description: Declared mutants of the audio Module (docs/architecture/target/v2/audio.zh-Hant.md), run with python3 tests/common/mutation/run_mutations.py --catalog docs/architecture/plans/audio/scripts/mutations.json --build-dir <build dir>. A mutant is killed only when its test run fails with the expected message. The SDL output backend's mutants left with the backend (v8-arch-gyo2-audio-review); the SDL batch sets up its own.

mutants.what: A voice starts one frame after its start frame
mutants.cases: *starts a clip exactly at its start frame*

mutants.what: The last frame of every internal pass is skipped, so the output depends on the block split
mutants.cases: *does not depend on how blocks split it*
mutants.expect: CHECK\( RenderInBlocks\(split, 2200, blocks\) == reference \) is NOT correct

mutants.what: A finished voice stays busy
mutants.find: if (voice.position >= voice.clip.frames || chunkStart + at >= voice.stopFrame) End(voice);
mutants.cases: *drops a play when every voice is busy*

mutants.what: A start before the next frame is counted as on time
mutants.cases: *starts a late play at the next frame*
mutants.expect: CHECK\( mixer.Schedule\(\{clip, 4, 1.0f, 1.0f\}\) == StartOutcome::Late \) is NOT correct

mutants.what: The mix truncates instead of rounding half up
mutants.cases: *applies left and right gains with rounding*

mutants.what: Saturated samples are not counted
Clip::Make accepts any sample rate
mutants.cases: *Clip rejects clips the mixer cannot play*

mutants.what: The mixer links another Engine library (GYO::Kernel): audio's links are exactly GYO::Base, GYO::Time and GYO::Asset
mutants.replace: target_link_libraries(gyo_audio PUBLIC GYO::Base GYO::Time PRIVATE GYO::Kernel)

mutants.what: A request is mapped without the block's start frame
mutants.cases: *maps a request in a later block*

mutants.what: Offsets are floored instead of rounded
mutants.expect: CHECK\( OnsetOf\(10'417, Duration::zero\(\)\) == 1 \) is NOT correct

mutants.what: Negative offsets round toward zero (integer division)
mutants.expect: CHECK\( OnsetOf\(-10'417, delay\) == 47 \) is NOT correct

mutants.what: Halves round away from zero (std::round) instead of toward +infinity
mutants.replace:
return ns >= 0 ? FloorDiv(ns * kFramesPerUnit + kNsPerUnit / 2, kNsPerUnit)
                   : -FloorDiv(-ns * kFramesPerUnit + kNsPerUnit / 2, kNsPerUnit);
mutants.expect: CHECK\( OnsetOf\(-31'250, delay\) == 47 \) is NOT correct

mutants.what: The schedule delay is truncated to frames
mutants.expect: CHECK\( OnsetOf\(0, Ns\(10'417\)\) == 1 \) is NOT correct

mutants.what: Offsets are clamped to a second instead of an hour
The positive overflow of at - anchor is not caught
mutants.find: if (b < 0 && a > std::numeric_limits<std::int64_t>::max() + b) return kMaxOffsetNs;

mutants.what: A full ring accepts one more request, overwriting the oldest
A request dropped by a full ring is not counted
The audio thread never frees the ring
Every submitter gets the first queue

A thread binding is put back into Submitter::Enqueue, which Play, Stop and StopAll share (the first thread to queue through a submitter claims it, another thread then asserts): the hand-over contract (one user at a time, ordered by happens-before) no longer holds. Only the three hand-over cases catch it.
mutants.cases: *plays on another thread after a hand-over*,*stops on another thread after a hand-over*,*plays on one thread and lets go on another after a hand-over*

mutants.what: The mix truncates instead of rounding half up
mutants.expect: CHECK\( hash.value == kRecordedHash \) is NOT correct

mutants.what: Render allocates and frees a block on the audio thread (an explicit ::operator new call, which the compiler may not elide; a dead std::vector is elided under optimization and allocates nothing)
A stop ends one frame late
mutants.cases: *stops a sound at the frame its time maps to*

mutants.what: A stop ignores its timestamp and applies at the block that takes it
A stop's frame leaves out the schedule delay
A stop stops every voice, not only its sound's
StopAll stops other submitters' sounds too
A sound stopped before its start keeps its voice until its start
A started sound stopped at an earlier time is treated as never started
A late stop is not counted late
A voice that reached its stop frame stays busy
mutants.find: if (voice.position >= voice.clip.frames || chunkStart + at >= voice.stopFrame) End(voice);
mutants.cases: *stops a sound at the frame its time maps to*

mutants.what: An unmatched stop is not counted
The sequence does not advance, so handles repeat
mutants.expect: CHECK\( a != b \) is NOT correct

mutants.what: The handle prefix has 6 bits, so the 64th submitter's prefix overflows
A voice whose start is the block's first frame counts as started
mutants.cases: *late play clamped to the block start*

mutants.what: A stop exactly at the block's first frame counts as late
mutants.cases: *frees a started sound stopped at the block*

mutants.what: A later stop replaces an earlier one
A voice whose stop frame ends the block stays busy into the next block
A handle with sequence 0 passes as issued
Render allocates while it applies a stop
mutants.find: const Detail::StopResult result = state.voices.Stop(command.handle, mask, stopFrame);

mutants.what: A voice that reaches its end or stop frame keeps its table entry, which never comes back
mutants.find: if (voice.position >= voice.clip.frames || chunkStart + at >= voice.stopFrame) End(voice);
mutants.replace: if (voice.position >= voice.clip.frames || chunkStart + at >= voice.stopFrame) voice.active = false;
mutants.cases: *on the submitter's next call after its play ended*
mutants.expect: CHECK\( next.frees == one \) is NOT correct

mutants.what: A voice freed by a stop before its start keeps its table entry, which never comes back
mutants.find: End(voice); // stopped before it started: never heard
mutants.cases: *on the submitter's next call after its play ended*
mutants.expect: CHECK\( next.frees == one \) is NOT correct

mutants.what: A started voice freed by a late stop keeps its table entry, which never comes back
mutants.replace:
if (stopFrame < nextFrame_) result.late = true;
            voice.active = false;
mutants.cases: *on the submitter's next call after its play ended*
mutants.expect: CHECK\( next.frees == one \) is NOT correct

mutants.what: Ended voices are handed back again at every later drain, so a reused entry comes back while its new play still sounds
mutants.cases: *does not hand a reused entry back early*

mutants.what: The ended list holds one voice, so a second voice ending in the same Render never hands its entry back
mutants.cases: *hands back every voice that ends in one block*
mutants.expect: CHECK\( call.frees == 2 \* one \) is NOT correct

mutants.what: Voices a stop frees are not drained before the next play reuses them, so the ended list overflows and entries are lost until the table runs out
mutants.cases: *hands back the entry of every voice a block frees*

mutants.what: The board writes a voice's new tag before its new state
mutants.expect: CHECK\( \(state == twoInit \|\| state == twoState\) \) is NOT correct

mutants.what: The reader does not read the tag again after the state
mutants.find: if (entry.tag.load(std::memory_order_acquire) != tag) return false; // reassigned: the sound ended
mutants.expect: CHECK\( state == oneState \) is NOT correct

mutants.what: Clear leaves the voice's tag
Assign writes the new state while the old tag is still there
mutants.expect: CHECK_FALSE\( found \) is NOT correct|CHECK\( state == oneState \) is NOT correct

mutants.what: An invalid handle matches an idle voice
A voice's position is published only when it is assigned
mutants.expect: CHECK\( playing.status == Playhead::Status::Playing \) is NOT correct

mutants.what: An ended voice keeps its published sound
mutants.expect: CHECK\( rig.mixer.PlayheadOf\(sound\).status == Playhead::Status::NotPlaying \) is NOT correct

mutants.what: A voice that starts at the next frame is reported playing
mutants.expect: CHECK\( rig.mixer.PlayheadOf\(sound\).status == Playhead::Status::Scheduled \) is NOT correct

mutants.what: A voice taken by another sound within one block is only published, so its old tag shows the new sound
mutants.cases: *taken by another sound within one block*
mutants.expect: CHECK\( rig.mixer.PlayheadOf\(a\).status == Playhead::Status::NotPlaying \) is NOT correct

mutants.what: The reader stops at the first voice whose tag does not match
The last voice is never published
A voice counts as started only after its second frame
mutants.expect: CHECK\( now.status == Playhead::Status::Playing \) is NOT correct

mutants.what: PlayheadOf reports every sound as not playing (block-by-block case)
A voice's position is published only when it is assigned (block-by-block case)
An ended voice keeps its published sound (block-by-block case)
PlayheadOf reports twice the position, past the clip's end (block-by-block case)
PlayheadOf reports every sound as not playing: the stress run never reaches its playing reads and is invalid (takes 3 x 20 s)
mutants.expect: CHECK\( track.playingReads >= kPlayingReads \) is NOT correct

mutants.what: PlayheadOf reports twice the position, past the clip's end (stress case, the secondary value checks)
The audio thread clears a playing sound's playhead after its first block instead of publishing its position (Fable check, place 1)
PlayheadOf reports NotPlaying at positions 128 and 384, then Playing again (the never-comes-back check; Fable check, place 2)
PlayheadOf reports the position modulo 128, so it goes back without passing the clip (the only-grows check; Fable check, place 3)

The audio thread reassigns every voice's board slot every block, so a concurrent reader can briefly see a playing sound as not playing (Fable check, place 4; concurrent only); v8-arch-gyo2-sdl-a added the long-sounds case, which polls only sounding sounds in a tight loop

Play counts the request before its empty-clip check, so a misused play is counted although it asserts (the Contract: Programmer Errors are asserted before anything is counted). Takes over from au-review-unload-counts-before-assert (UnloadClip is gone).

The audio thread hands a play's entry back as soon as the play is taken, also when it gets a voice: the producer lets go of the clip while the voice still reads it (too early; the caller let go already).
mutants.cases: *on the submitter's next call after its play ended*

mutants.what: A stop at a later frame hands the voice's entry back when it is taken, before the voice reaches that frame (too early).
mutants.find: voice.stopFrame = std::min(voice.stopFrame, stopFrame); // the earliest stop wins
mutants.replace:
voice.stopFrame = std::min(voice.stopFrame, stopFrame); // the earliest stop wins
        if (voice.lease != 0 && endedCount_ < ended_.size()) ended_[endedCount_++] = voice.lease;
mutants.cases: *on the submitter's next call after its play ended*

mutants.what: A play dropped for want of a voice never hands its entry back, so its clip stays held and the table shrinks.
mutants.cases: *takes its table and both rings around twice*
mutants.expect: CHECK\( stop.frees == one \) is NOT correct

mutants.what: Taking back an entry does not let go of its clip: the mixer holds every clip it ever played until its state goes.
mutants.find: slot.held[entry] = Clip{}; // may let go of the last reference, here and never on the audio thread
mutants.cases: *lets go of the clips handed back on each of its calls*
mutants.expect: CHECK\( call.frees == one \) is NOT correct

mutants.what: Play does not take back the handed-back entries first (only Stop, StopAll and the destructor do).
mutants.cases: *takes its table and both rings around twice*
mutants.expect: CHECK\( call.frees == \(pending \? one : 0\) \) is NOT correct

mutants.what: A play the full queue drops lets go of its clip but does not put its entry back on the stack, so repeated drops use the table up.
mutants.cases: *the full queue dropped in that call*

mutants.what: The lease mark keeps only 16 bits of the table entry (as the old clip-slot mark did), so an entry above 65535 comes back as another entry.
mutants.cases: *hands an entry above 65535 back to its own submitter*
mutants.expect: CHECK\( call.frees == one \) is NOT correct

mutants.what: Play copies the clip's samples into the table instead of sharing them (an allocation on the producer for every play).
mutants.cases: *lets go of the clips handed back on each of its calls*

mutants.what: Clip::Make(vector&&) copies the samples instead of taking them.
mutants.cases: *copies samples given as a span once and shares them from then on*
mutants.expect: CHECK\( taken->View\(\).samples.data\(\) == data \) is NOT correct

mutants.what: The loader hands Clip::Make 48000 instead of the file's sample rate (master's SoundLoader never checked the rate)
The loader does not check 16 bits per sample
The loader does not check the format tag (integer PCM)
The loader does not check the block align
The loader accepts a data chunk of an odd number of bytes (the last byte is dropped)
A chunk that runs past the end is reported as a missing chunk
mutants.expect: CHECK\( loaded.error\(\).code == code \) is NOT correct

mutants.what: The loader accepts a second fmt or data chunk
The loader does not skip the pad byte after an odd chunk
mutants.cases: *the pad byte and the short tail*
mutants.expect: CHECK\( Load\(Riff\(\{Chunk\("LIST", Bytes\(3, std::byte\{7\}\)\), Fmt\(\), Data\(kStereo\)\}\)\).has_value\(\) \) is NOT correct

mutants.what: Play queues the clip's view without keeping a reference in the table, so a play outlives its samples once the caller lets go (only the table keeps them alive while the audio thread reads them).
mutants.cases: *on the submitter's next call after its play ended*
mutants.expect: CHECK\( next.frees == one \) is NOT correct
